hints: In equilibrium on the $20^\circ$ slope, friction balances the downhill component of gravity.
Calculate the downhill component of weight: $F = mg\sin 20^\circ$ with $m = 0.2\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the plane for equilibrium:
$$F = mg\sin 20^\circ = 0.2(10)\sin 20^\circ = 2\sin 20^\circ$$

Evaluate the friction force to 3 significant figures:
$$F = 2(0.342020) \approx 0.684\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Friction on Inclined Planes: Uses the perpendicular reaction and friction $F=\mu R$ opposing the motion on the plane, obtaining The friction force is 0.684 N (3 s.f.).

teacher_walkthrough: The particle of mass $m = 0.2\text{ kg}$ rests in equilibrium on the rough plane inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal.
Because the particle is stationary with no other external forces acting along the slope, static friction must balance the component of the particle's weight directed down the slope:

Resolve along the slope:
$$F = mg\sin 20^\circ$$
$$F = 0.2 \times 10 \times \sin 20^\circ = 2\sin 20^\circ$$
$$F \approx 2 \times 0.342020 = 0.68404\text{ N} \approx 0.684\text{ N}$$

hints: Calculate limiting friction opposing downward motion: $F = \mu R = 0.6(2\cos 20^\circ) \approx 1.128\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law down the slope: $0.9 + 0.2g\sin 20^\circ - F = 0.2a$, and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Calculate normal reaction perpendicular to the incline:
$$R = mg\cos 20^\circ = 0.2(10)\cos 20^\circ = 2\cos 20^\circ \approx 1.8794\text{ N}$$

Calculate the limiting frictional force opposing downward sliding:
$$F = \mu R = 0.6(1.8794) \approx 1.1276\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law down the plane:
$$0.9 + mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$$
$$0.9 + 0.68404 - 1.12763 = 0.2a \implies 0.45641 = 0.2a$$

Solve for acceleration:
$$a = \frac{0.45641}{0.2} \approx 2.28\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ down the plane}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Friction on Inclined Planes: Uses $R = 0.2g \cos 20^\circ$, obtaining The acceleration is 2.28 $m\,s^{-2}$ down the plane.

teacher_walkthrough: A downward force of $0.9\text{ N}$ is applied to the particle along the line of greatest slope.

Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find the normal reaction $R$:
$$R = mg\cos 20^\circ = 0.2 \times 10 \times \cos 20^\circ = 2\cos 20^\circ \approx 1.879385\text{ N}$$

Since the particle moves down the plane, friction opposes this motion by acting up the plane with limiting magnitude:
$$F = \mu R = 0.6 \times 1.879385 \approx 1.12763\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) down the incline:
$$F_{\text{applied}} + mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$$
$$0.9 + 0.68404 - 1.12763 = 0.2a$$
$$0.45641 = 0.2a$$
$$a = \frac{0.45641}{0.2} \approx 2.282\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 2.28\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ down the plane}$$
